rows.backtranslation: Choose an image format and its settings for reducing file size. Save will reuse this file name, this location, this format and these settings.
rows.context_and_review_note: Exact-base SaveOptionsDialog.kt:52/:183 shows this non-export/non-share help. ClassicPaintActivity.kt:1104-1108 reuses savedTarget.uri and savedTarget.options; :1370 establishes SavedTarget(uri,name,options) after ordinary save. Revised uncertain compression coinage into settings for reducing file size. This is a descriptive compression paraphrase, not image dimensions or a promise of lossless encoding. All four reuse dimensions and exact Save label are retained. Bound-state coordinated nouns reviewed.

rows.english: Higher quality preserves more detail and usually makes a larger file.
rows.value: ⵓⴳⴳⴰⵔ ⵏ ⵜⵖⴰⵔⴰ ⴷⴰ ⵉⵃⵟⵟⵓ ⵓⴳⴳⴰⵔ ⵏ ⵉⴼⵔⵓⵔⵉⵜⵏ. ⴳ ⵜⵓⴳⵜⵜ ⵏ ⵜⵉⴽⴽⴰⵍ, ⴷⴰ ⵉⵎⵖⵓⵔ ⵓⴼⴰⵢⵍⵓ.
rows.backtranslation: More quality preserves more details. Most often, the file grows.
rows.context_and_review_note: Exact-base SaveOptionsDialog.kt:102 uses this for JPEG/HEIC quality help. Retained higher quality, more details and most-often file growth. The preceding quality statement supplies the comparison; it does not say quality is lossless, that output is always larger, or that existing files grow by themselves. No guaranteed recovery of details already lost is claimed.

rows.english: Higher quality usually makes a larger file. Lossless keeps every colour value.
rows.value: ⵓⴳⴳⴰⵔ ⵏ ⵜⵖⴰⵔⴰ ⴷⴰ ⵉⵙⵙⵉⵎⵖⵓⵔ ⴰⴼⴰⵢⵍⵓ ⴳ ⵜⵓⴳⵜⵜ ⵏ ⵜⵉⴽⴽⴰⵍ. ⴰⵏⴰⵡ ⵏⵏⴰ ⵉⵃⵟⵟⵓⵏ ⵉⵙⴼⴽⴰ ⵏ ⵉⴷ ⴱⵉⴽⵙⵍ ⴰⴽⴽⵯ ⴷⴰ ⵉⵃⵟⵟⵓ ⴽⵓ ⴰⵣⴰⵍ ⵏ ⵓⴽⵍⵓ.
rows.backtranslation: More quality usually makes the file larger. The mode that preserves all pixel data preserves every colour value.
rows.context_and_review_note: Exact-base SaveOptionsDialog.kt:87-89 controls the lossless checkbox and quality slider; :103 selects this description for the remaining formats, with PNG explanation hidden at :105. Retained descriptive lossless mode: all pixel data, every colour value. Pixel qualifier prevents an all-file-data/metadata preservation promise. Higher-quality/larger-file relation remains qualified as usual, not universal. Anaw is used descriptively for encoding type/mode, not a claim all encodings of the format are lossless.
